description: Existing semantic context module data; consumed through the unified module-data registry.

semantic_request_markers_v1.description: Generic recipient-directed request or instruction markers. These classify speech acts only and must not create threat evidence by themselves.

semantic_instruction_markers_v1.description: Markers that distinguish a stronger instruction from an ordinary request. They classify speech acts only and never create threat evidence by themselves.

semantic_anti_action_markers_v1.description: Local anti-action and warning markers. They qualify only the bounded sentence or span in which they occur.

semantic_report_markers_v1.description: Markers that suggest a report, case study, or incident description rather than a current recipient instruction.
items: การฝึกอบรมความปลอดภัย

semantic_action_markers_v1.description: Common action predicates used to build semantic claims. They classify an action and do not create threat evidence alone.
items: เข้าสู่ระบบ

semantic_object_markers_v1.description: Objects of common email actions. These are semantic attributes, not standalone threat keywords.

semantic_quote_markers_v1.description: Structural markers for quoted, forwarded, or reported message sections. They set context only and do not create threat evidence.

semantic_clause_markers_v2.description: Boundaries between locally attributed action clauses. Each resulting clause retains source offsets and its own action/polarity; this policy creates no threat by itself.

semantic_description_markers_v2.description: Description/mention tails are observations and cannot borrow a preceding request marker as execution authority.

semantic_self_subject_markers_v2.description: Legacy clause-initial first-person action subjects retained as explicit sender speaker prefixes. A separate local target policy proves recipient, sender_self, or unknown.

semantic_third_party_subject_markers_v2.description: Explicit third-party action subjects; these do not establish current recipient instructions.

semantic_imperative_prefixes_v2.description: Explicit recipient-directed command prefixes used without a separate politeness marker. Generic isolated action verbs remain observations.

semantic_forward_end_markers_v2.description: Structural whole-line endings of quoted/forwarded scope. Ordinary mentions do not open or close quotation scope.

semantic_html_quote_classes_v2.description: Structural quoted-message HTML container classes. The container boundary, not a prose substring, establishes quoted source scope.

semantic_recipient_directed_markers_v2.description: Explicit speaker requests for the addressee to act, distinguished from first-person self-action descriptions.

semantic_nominal_html_cta_markers_v2.description: Nominal informational/authentication button labels are recipient action facts only with their own physical HTML href or submit/formaction carrier in the same bounded source span. Plain mentions or another button target supply no authority.

semantic_first_person_subject_prefixes_v.description: Explicit clause-initial first-person speaker forms prove the sender actor only. They do not prove recipient direction or object ownership.

semantic_recipient_target_markers_v2.description: Explicit recipient pronouns used only as a bounded first action argument in a first-person assertion. They never create a recipient instruction.

semantic_sender_self_target_markers_v2.description: Explicit first-person reflexive or direct object forms used as a bounded first action argument; speaker identity alone cannot prove sender_self.

semantic_recipient_possessive_markers_v2.description: Recipient ownership requires an explicit possessive before the first following semantic object. Later recipient mentions cannot reassign a sender-owned object.

semantic_sender_possessive_markers_v2.description: Sender ownership requires an explicit possessive before the first following semantic object; generic first-person action subjects remain target unknown.

semantic_url_intro_markers_v2.description: Exact neutral details-introduction lines allowed only in a bounded unique physical URL continuation of an already qualified current details action. A same-sentence configured completion/courtesy tail may intervene; blank lines, quotes, forward headers, other objects or another URL block the relation.

semantic_url_pointer_actions_v2.description: Action roles compatible with a nearby explicit details pointer. Every action in the pointer claim must match; these words do not create a request or threat alone.

semantic_url_pointer_objects_v2.description: Affected objects compatible with an explicit details pointer. A credential, account, invoice or other object cannot borrow this pointer's physical URL.

semantic_url_pointer_completion_tails_v2.description: Exact generic completion tails permitted inside the same bounded sentence after a qualified details request. Tail claims must be original current recipient actions with no different semantic object.

semantic_url_pointer_courtesy_tails_v2.description: Optional exact courtesy suffixes following a configured same-sentence completion tail. They do not supply action, actor, object or URL authority.

semantic_context_guard_policy_v1.description: Local lexical and attribution guards. Exclusions are occurrence-scoped; destinations are action arguments, not speaker identities.

semantic_request_construction_policy_v1.description: Stage B request constructions. `stage_b_enabled` supersedes the legacy `enabled` flag so persisted seeds receive the activation through additive backfill; set it to false to disable. Reuses existing action/object lists; never directly scores threats.

semantic_discussion_action_markers_v1.description: Requested explanation/inspection predicates. Complement actions are topics, not instructions to execute.
